title: ADR-0021 Amendment 4 attributes an inert-comparison defect to a lore-cli citation-name validator that has never existed in this repository
description:
ADR-0021 Amendment 4 is binding on opum-doc main (6e1c5844f76f6c3e9b2312ce4879f0547eb121cf, "docs(ODOC-236):
Amendment 4 -- the citation name must contain a hyphen (#357)") and contains a statement about THIS
repository that this repository cannot substantiate. Filed so the claim is answerable from a record rather
than from a session's memory of a message. NOT lore-cli work to do: the correction is opum-doc's record and
opum-agent's ruling. Informational, awaiting the orchestrator's decision.

WHAT AMENDMENT 4 SAYS. Under "Why mandate a shape rather than keep enumerating", defect 2 (the inert
comparison -- an uppercase reserved-name list tested against a lowercase-only charset, so a literal
membership test matches nothing) is recorded as: "Real, and deliberately not in this record. It is a
lore-cli implementation defect, in lore-cli's citation-name validator, and it was excluded from ODOC-231 at
the time because it is implementation rather than design and lore-cli was already fixing it." Its cited
record is OPAG-212 on opum-agent main at 0e2d33d, which reads "lore-cli's independent catch, NOT ruled
because it is implementation and it is already fixing it".

WHAT IS MEASURABLY HERE, all against origin/dev a94bf095 unless stated.
1. There is no citation-name validator in this repository. `git log --all -S"citationName" -- src/` returns
   nothing, and so does the same pickaxe for `COM1`. Not on dev, not on main, and there are no other remote
   branches -- `git ls-remote --heads origin` lists only dev, main, and the LCLI-540 branch.
2. There is no reserved device-name list in src/ in EITHER case. Grepped for "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL",
   COM1, LPT1 and their lowercase forms. The only RESERVED_* constants here are RESERVED_STEMS
   (index/log, src/core/scaffold.ts:56), RESERVED_FILES (src/core/indexes.ts:65), RESERVED_FIELDS
   (src/core/profile.ts:776) and RESERVED_ROOT_INDEX (src/commands/new.ts:43). All unrelated.
3. (2) is the load-bearing one, not (1): AN INERT COMPARISON REQUIRES A LIST TO COMPARE AGAINST. No list of
   any case exists anywhere in src/, so the defect as described cannot be present regardless of what a
   validator might be named. Stating it this way because (1) alone would be a search-coverage argument and
   could be wrong if the symbol is named something I did not guess.
4. Consistent with the ADR's own framing at line 46 -- the ruling was free because "no user-chosen snapshot
   name exists anywhere". Confirmed at the surface: src/commands/snapshot.ts rejects a positional on
   `retain` (:53-56, "snapshot retain accepts no snapshot key, --all, or --workspace-id") and on `list`
   (:70-71), and the single positional `delete` accepts (:79-83) is a snapshot KEY digest normalized by
   normalizeSnapshotKey, not a user-chosen name. So opum-doc's narrowing to delete-only is right, and
   narrower still than "delete accepts a name".

WHAT THIS REPOSITORY ACTUALLY CAUGHT, which is the likely origin of the drift: a DESIGN observation about
the ADR's own ruled list -- that an uppercase list against a lowercase-only charset would be inert WHEN
IMPLEMENTED -- i.e. a prediction about a future implementation, not a report of shipped code. Between that
catch and Amendment 4 it became a defect in a validator plus a claim that this repository was already
fixing it. Nothing here is being fixed, because nothing here is broken in that way.

OPEN QUESTION PUT TO opum-agent (design, so not decided here): does ruling 11 reach existing name surfaces,
or only the future user-chosen snapshot name? The nearest real surfaces are
src/core/workspace-contract.ts:45 (/^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9._-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$/u -- bounded both ends, no
leading hyphen, but permits "." and "_" and does not require a hyphen) and src/core/agent-profile.ts:45
(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/). If ruling 11 governs only the future surface, there is no lore-cli work
under it today and this task closes as informational.
